subject: Business Models
title: Territory Rights
description: A fast breakdown of Territory Rights for builders.

hook.text: You buy a Subway franchise. Then Subway opens another location 2 blocks away. Your sales drop 30%.

buildup.text: Territory rights define the geographic area where no other franchisee can operate the same brand.

discovery.text: Exclusive territories protect franchisees. Non-exclusive ones let the franchisor saturate an area for more fees.

twist.text: Subway infamously over-saturated markets. At one point, there were more Subways than McDonald's in the US.

climax.text: Territory disputes are among the most common franchise lawsuits. This clause matters enormously.

punchline.text: No territory protection means competing with your own brand. Read the contract.

quiz.question: What problem does territory exclusivity solve?
options: Preventing brand cannibalization from nearby same-brand locations

details.summary: Territory rights define the geographic area where a franchisee has exclusive or protected rights to operate. Exclusive territories guarantee no other franchisee of the same brand will open nearby, while non-exclusive arrangements allow the franchisor to place additional units at their discretion.
details.whyItMatters: Territory rights determine a franchisee's revenue potential and competitive protection. Weak territory protections allow franchisors to open new locations nearby that cannibalize existing sales.
takeaways: Exclusive territories protect franchisees from same-brand competition nearby
Non-exclusive territories allow franchisors to add locations at their discretion
Territory definitions in contracts determine long-term revenue potential and risk

faq.question: What types of territory protections exist in franchise agreements?
faq.answer: Exclusive territories prohibit any same-brand units within defined boundaries. Protected territories limit new units but allow exceptions. Non-exclusive territories provide no protection. Some agreements protect physical stores but allow online sales or delivery into the territory.

faq.question: How should franchisees evaluate territory rights before signing?
faq.answer: Calculate the population and commercial density within the territory. Research the franchisor's history of encroachment complaints. Verify whether online and delivery sales are included in territory protections. Consult a franchise attorney to assess the specific contractual language.
